host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.note: This is not the gfx1100 W7900 that docs/PLAN.md names as the default target; every figure here is a gfx1151 measurement.

change: K and Q are loaded eight (K) and four (Q) elements per instruction instead of one. A lane owns one key, so the scalar K walk asked the L1 for 32 sectors per request -- lanes land head_dim*2 bytes apart -- 128 times per tile.
The V walk is split at the AR/NAR boundary and steps by pointer instead of multiplying and branching per key.
Per-row arithmetic is unchanged: the same d-ascending dot product, the same tile walk, the same key-ascending accumulation order.

production_shape_call.note: Median of 6 batches of 5 calls. The R=4 packed version measured 33900 us, R=16 44900 us and R=32 88500 us, so 8 is the measured optimum on this host.

rocprofv3_pmc.command: rocprofv3 --pmc GRBM_COUNT SQ_WAVES_sum SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_INSTS_LDS SQ_INSTS_FLAT OccupancyPercent --output-format csv -d <dir> -- python3 scripts/yue2_attention_bench.py --repeat 1 --warmup 1
rocprofv3_pmc.reading: The parent kernel was not bandwidth-bound as its comment claimed: 3.5e8 cycles carried 3.7e9 VALU instructions at 19% occupancy, i.e. it was stalled. Packing the loads cut global requests per lane-tile 740 -> 385 and the row blocking raised achieved occupancy to 93%; the kernel is now VALU-issue-bound at roughly 60% of peak issue.

bit_parity.result: bit-identical to the parent kernel (max abs diff 0.0)
bit_parity.note: The fixture's 6-row / 192-AR-row shape exercises the partial last row block. A second, deliberate perturbation of the scalar fallback fails the head_dim=100 case and passes head_dim=128, so the new fallback test is load-bearing.

unit_tests.note: New parametrization over head_dim in {128, 100} covers the packed path and the scalar fallback.

replay_same_protocol.note: Both arms were run on the same host in the same session, one after the other, with the gate's own JSON as the source of every number.

replay_product_steps.note: The 'before' arm is the same case at the same step count recorded in benchmarks/results/yue2_m7_attention_20260917.json, whose nar_seconds is its 465.9 s replay total minus its 22.47 s decode. The 2-step run's attention-only extrapolation to 32 steps (about 178 s) over-predicted, because part of the 2-step non-attention time is per-replay rather than per-evaluation; this is the measured figure.

nar_stage_split.method: hipengine.kernels.hip_gfx1100.yue2.nar.nar_attention_f32 wrapped with a device synchronize on either side, run over Yue2NarRuntime.synthesize for the same case
nar_stage_split.reading: Attention was ~18.5 s of the 27.76 s solve and is now 2.93 s, so the NAR's remaining cost is its projections (hipBLASLt GEMMs, RoPE, norms), not the solver's attention.

parity_gates_after_change.e2e_case_shape: frames 1297/1297, samples 2490176/2490176, peak 0.9457, determinism bit-identical, torch imported: False
parity_gates_after_change.m4_solver_gate: unchanged; the kernel's per-row arithmetic and the parent-bits fixture are the same

next_candidates: NAR projections: 8.18 s of the 11.11 s 2-step solve, 1 494 hipBLASLt dispatches per replay of a 32x32 macro-tile kernel for shapes this large. At 32 steps the solve is 116.53 s against the reference's 27.32 s, and this is where most of that gap now sits.
VAE decode: 20.07 s of the 31.10 s replay, dominated by yue2_vae_conv1d_f32_kernel and yue2_vae_conv_transpose1d_f32_kernel.
Attention tile maximum via a warp shuffle (fmax is order-independent, so it stays bit-exact): each lane still walks 128 shared-memory entries serially per tile per row.
